concerns.text: T002's verification requires pytest to pass 'on real signal traces', but no task before T002 produces real torque/velocity traces — T001 only fetches the DragMesh-2 manifest (geometry, not per-timestep torque logs), and the simulation environment that logs `torque_hand`/`velocity_object` is built in T004. This is a consumer-before-producer dependency: either move the real-trace verification into/after T004, or restrict T002's verification to synthetic fixtures and add a real-trace validation step post-T004.

T004's smoke run writes trial rows to `data/results/sweep.csv`, T005 appends to the same file ('append mode, no full in-memory accumulation'), and T007 fits the GLMM 'on the trial rows from data/results/sweep.csv'. The smoke rows (2 objects, 'a few episodes') will contaminate the full-study analysis unless T005 explicitly resets/filters the file. Add an explicit step in T005 to start from a clean `sweep.csv` (or tag rows with a run_id the analysis filters on) so T007 consumes only full-run trials.

FR-002/FR-011 map k_norm to percentiles 'within the training distribution', but no task produces a training-distribution k_norm reference (friction ∈ [0.2,0.6]) before the adaptive policy runs in T004/T005 — T003 is unit-tested on synthetic thresholds and T004/T005 evaluate only on novel out-of-range objects. The adaptive policy in T005 has no producer for its percentile baseline; add a task (or extend T004/T005) to collect k_norm statistics on training-range friction objects before the adaptive policy is evaluated.
